A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAL research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V4 reports original synthetic bandit simulations, evaluations on nine real-world benchmarks, and a drift-radius experiment in Figures 1–3.

after.justification: V5 retains original synthetic and real-world evaluations and additionally reports GSR detector comparisons and computational runtime results.

M1.justification: V5 adds GSR as an implemented detector option, accumulating likelihood ratios alongside the existing GLR rule. The DAL wrapper and stationary learners are retained. Algorithm 1 also corrects the exploration-index offset.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five bandit families, geometric change-point scenarios, linear drift, random drift-radius scenarios, and nine real-world benchmarks. The added detector and runtime comparisons reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: V5 Figure 1 substantially expands the synthetic comparisons with curves labeled Discounted, Sliding-Window, Budget-Restart, and BVD-GLM-UCB. These supplement the retained MASTER, WeightUCB, ADA-OPKB, WGP-UCB, and ADA-ILTCB+ comparisons; they are evaluated additions, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: V5 adds runtime in seconds as an evaluation metric, averaged across piecewise-stationary and drifting simulations in Figure 2, and specifies configurations for the new GSR evaluations. Existing horizons, action/context dimensions, drift schedules, and real-world evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: V5 adds systematic GLR-versus-GSR comparisons across synthetic and real-world settings and a runtime analysis across bandit families, testing detector sensitivity and computational practicality. The existing drift-radius robustness experiment is retained as Figure 4. The new appendix discussion of covering-set sensitivity is explanatory, not another empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 15 independent synthetic trials and 15 real-world runs and display variability graphically. V5 adds no disclosed seed lists, confidence-interval definitions, significance tests, or revised uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V5 adds GSR performance curves, results for the expanded synthetic comparator set, and per-family runtime measurements. For example, Figure 2 reports LB runtimes of 3.79 seconds for DAL-GLR, 3.76 for DAL-GSR, and 15.81 for MASTER. It reports a slight GSR advantage while retaining the broad DAL performance ranking; these additions do not establish a same-setting improvement over v4.

T1.justification: V5 replaces the GLR-specific Theorem 4.4 with detector-general Theorem 4.8 using Property 4.1, explicitly requires increasing and concave stationary regret bounds, and revises contextual sampling/separation requirements in Definition 4.5. Appendix B.5 substantially develops the false-alarm, delayed-detection, concentration, and regret arguments beyond v4's proof sketch. The headline regret rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: V5 narrows the title, abstract, and conclusion framing from general non-stationary to piecewise stationary bandits and makes the optimal-stationary-regret qualification explicit in the abstract. It strengthens the detector-general and 'detect-the-model' novelty claims while retaining the main empirical dominance and regret-rate contributions.

C2.justification: V5 interprets the similar GLR/GSR results as evidence that performance comes from DAL's design rather than one detector. It adds explanations of covering-set cost, structural complexity, and RKHS smoothness, plus interpretation of runtime competitiveness. The limitations concerning drifting guarantees and change-point separation are retained.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly supplies practical GLR/GSR thresholds and δF = T^(-1/2), whereas v4 deferred practical detector tuning to cited work. V5 also corrects an extra information-gain factor in the finite-kernel covering-set instructions. These disclosures do not establish that retained experiments were rerun; hardware and stated dataset-access arrangements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V5 adds Boutron et al. (2020) and removes references to Lefortier et al. (2014), Luo et al. (2018), and Wu et al. (2018). The introduction sharpens the contrast with earlier regret-bound detectors and adds the cited 143-billion-round criticism of MASTER. Most research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: V5 substantially reorganizes the experimental narrative into baseline, tuning, synthetic, and real-world subsections, condenses benchmark descriptions, and restructures the theoretical exposition around explicit definitions and assumptions. Detector material is redistributed between the main text and appendices, alongside extensive prose editing.

P2.justification: V5 changes the main paper to a two-column conference layout, enlarges and recolors comparison plots, expands their legends, and adds runtime Figure 2. New main-text Table 1 summarizes existing regret comparisons; v4's detailed Table 1 remains as v5 Table 2. Appendix dataset plots are retained and rearranged.

improvement.justification: V5 substantially strengthens the support and auditability of central claims. Revised contextual separation conditions and the detailed Appendix B.5 argument address v4's abbreviated theoretical treatment, while detector comparisons and measured runtimes directly test modularity and practicality. Broader novelty wording and grouped baseline labels reduce precision, but the gains in theoretical documentation and empirical support outweigh these limitations.
